strengths: Novel dual-memory architecture with well-motivated design: gated global memory for long-range dependencies and FIFO temporary memory for recent context effectively address limitations of prior finite-state models

Remarkable empirical results: achieves 100% accuracy retrieving passkeys across all positions in 1M-token sequences despite training only on 32k contexts; matches fine-tuned full-attention performance on SCROLLS summarization tasks
Comprehensive experimental validation spanning academic benchmarks (SCROLLS with 7 diverse tasks), synthetic tasks (passkey), and real-world applications (user behavior QA, agent tasks)

Significant practical efficiency: maintains constant ~10GB memory footprint and stable ~22ms decode latency regardless of context length; achieves 21× speedup and 10× memory reduction versus full attention at 1M tokens
Valuable methodological contribution: layer-level pipeline parallelism yields 2.7× training speedup over naive context parallelism, enabling 128k context fine-tuning on 16×80GB GPUs
Practical plug-and-play integration into pre-trained models with minimal fine-tuning (3 epochs on 32k contexts); parameter-efficient design using low-rank adapters
Strong ablation studies (Figure 8) clearly demonstrating distinct roles of global versus temporary memory components, with gating visualization providing interpretability (Figures 10-11)
Clear presentation with well-designed architectural diagrams, comprehensive experimental tables, and detailed efficiency analysis comparing prefill/decode phases
weaknesses: Complexity claims overstated: terminology 'constant memory usage' misleading—method uses bounded fixed-size memory (~2.5k tokens), which is better than linear but not asymptotically constant; no formal proofs or rigorous complexity analysis provided; missing approximation error analysis
Limited model scale: experiments exclusively on Qwen3-4B; no validation on larger models (13B, 70B+) standard in modern NLP; generalization to different model architectures unexplored
Training scope limitations: fine-tuning only on 32k contexts; sensitivity to different training lengths unexplored; unclear how performance scales with variable training sequence lengths

Statistical rigor gaps: no confidence intervals, significance tests, or error bars reported; some SCROLLS differences appear within noise margins (e.g., 62.5 vs 61.0); Table 7 shows memory sensitivity but boundary conditions not explored

Reproducibility concerns: proprietary datasets (e-commerce UQA, Long-Horizon Agent Dataset) prevent independent validation; code link not provided; hyperparameter justification sparse (e.g., rank=8 for RLA); domain-specific real-world evaluation

Incomplete baseline coverage: missing recent strong methods (StreamingLLM, advanced positional interpolation approaches); memory budget alignment (~3k tokens) for all methods not rigorously justified; limited comparison with linear attention variants

Passkey task limitations: impressive extrapolation result but synthetic benchmark tests position-bias robustness in isolation rather than comprehensive long-context understanding; 1M extrapolation doesn't necessarily validate semantic understanding at extreme lengths

Technical details underspecified: gradient flow through parallel memory paths in update mechanism unexplained; FIFO queue design not compared against attention-based or learned selection; compression token interleaving strategy not ablated; computational overhead of gating mechanism not analyzed

Real-world evaluation concerns: UQA improvement (78.7 vs 76.0) lacks error bars; agent task evaluated on single recent benchmark (Terminal-Bench) with limited community establishment; results may not generalize beyond tested domains

Missing ablations and analyses: no systematic extrapolation degradation curves (32k→64k/256k); failure mode analysis absent; information retention rates across memory components not quantified; training efficiency (not just inference) incompletely evaluated

strengths: Well-motivated practical problem with high relevance to LLM deployment; quadratic complexity and linear KV cache growth are genuine bottlenecks
Novel dual-memory architecture with clear separation of concerns: gated global memory for long-range dependencies, FIFO temporary memory for recent details; design is well-justified
Remarkable extrapolation capability: trained on 32k contexts, accurately retrieves information from 1M tokens with 21× speedup and 10× memory reduction

Comprehensive experimental evaluation across multiple dimensions: academic benchmarks (SCROLLS with 7 tasks, 2WikiMQA, HotpotQA), synthetic tasks (passkey retrieval), real-world applications (UQA, Terminal-Bench)
Strong empirical results: matches or exceeds full attention on summarization tasks; outperforms all evaluated efficient baselines on average SCROLLS score (40.10 vs 38.24 for SWA)
Thorough ablation studies and analysis: memory allocation effects (Figure 7-8), RLA rank sensitivity, hyperparameter exploration, gating value visualization providing interpretability
Layer-level pipeline parallelism is novel and practical contribution enabling 128k training on 16×80GB GPUs with 2.7× speedup over naive context parallelism
Generalization demonstrated across model families and scales (Qwen3-4B, Qwen3-14B, Llama-3.1-8B) with consistent improvements
Parameter-efficient design with only 0.098% overhead; honest treatment of limitations and failure modes in appendix
weaknesses: Inconsistent performance across tasks: notable gaps on Qasper (35.5 vs 40.3 F1) and QALT (56.0 vs 64.2 F1) without full explanation; information aggregation failures indicate architectural limitations on reasoning tasks
Counterintuitive result on Llama-3.1-8B (CoMeT 104.6% of full attention) raises questions about whether improvements reflect method quality or training dynamics; insufficient analysis of this anomaly

Limited theoretical analysis: claimed O(1) space and O(N) time complexity lack formal proofs; no formalization of when/why gating preserves information; comparison with information-theoretic limits is qualitative

Incomplete baseline comparisons: InfiniAttention (cited but not compared as baseline); RWKV7 shows faster prefill in appendix but deserves main text discussion; limited comparison with state-space models despite extensive related work discussion

Reproducibility concerns: code URL missing despite availability statement; RLA and gate initialization schemes not detailed; training procedures for real-world datasets sparsely described; mixed dataset construction requires external datasets
Fine-tuning requirement moderates 'plug-and-play' claim: requires 3 epochs on mixed dataset, whereas compression methods need no fine-tuning; this trade-off should be more explicitly acknowledged

Model-dependent generalization: performance gap between Qwen and Llama varies substantially, raising questions about robustness; Terminal-Bench limited to 8B model (4B lacks 'fundamental capabilities') limits small-model applicability
Fundamental architectural limitation on aggregation: failure case 00da reveals inherent weakness in gathering information from non-contiguous parts; this isn't tunable and limits reasoning capability

Design choices not thoroughly justified: RLA rank=8 chosen despite small performance variation (Table 6); FIFO queue simplicity vs learned replacement policies not compared; compression token interval (every 8 tokens) appears arbitrary
Missing statistical significance testing and error bars; performance differences are sometimes modest, particularly on shorter sequences
